source.title: Revealing emergent human-like conceptual representations from language prediction
source.authors: Ningyu Xu; Qi Zhang; Chao Du; Qiang Luo; Xipeng Qiu; Xuanjing Huang; Menghan Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present; the text is not visibly cut off or garbled.
record.tranche_reason: It tests representational convergence using RSA and parallelism measures, and relates cross-model alignment to model performance and complexity. This is a conceptual test rather than a reproduction of the original method.
record.gate_note: The study reports representation-alignment results across demonstration contexts and across language models. Human-behavior and brain-encoding results are not rows because they do not measure convergence between AI models. The model-complexity trend is reported qualitatively, while exact cross-model alignment values are not supplied for individual models.
record.test_reason: Section 2.3 compares RSA alignment of concept representations across 67 open-source base LLMs that differ in family, scale and training data. It relates each model's alignment with LLaMA3-70B to accuracy and to a complexity index, which bears on V1. The method (reverse-dictionary concept representations, Spearman-RSA, one reference model) differs from the original's mutual-kNN approach. The authors frame the result as consistent with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors make two separate convergence claims: (a) within a model, representations derived under different contexts converge to a context-independent structure; (b) across LLMs, better-performing, higher-complexity models share more similar relational structure, which they say aligns with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. The record merges these into one. The authors also stress that the representations lack visually grounded perceptual properties such as color, texture and shape.
record.recipe_differences: Uses reverse-dictionary-derived conceptual representations and RSA/parallelism comparisons across contexts and models; it does not reproduce the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis measurement or its cross-modal paired-image-caption setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment changes with the number of contextual demonstrations, increasing from one to 24 and showing marginal gains beyond that point. The increase is also observed with cosine-based RSA and parallelism score, not only the primary Spearman-based RSA.

fits_no_version.finding: Within LLaMA3-70B, the relational structure of concept representations converges as in-context demonstrations increase. Against the 120-demo space: Spearman-RSA 0.800→0.970, cosine-RSA 0.759→0.962, parallelism score 0.840→0.974, each from 1 to 24 demos, with gains marginal after 24. Alignment tracks exact-match accuracy (ρ=0.976).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single LLM's representational geometry for concepts becomes context-invariant with sufficient in-context demonstrations, robustly across similarity metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: LLaMA3-70B concept representations predict human similarity judgments and fMRI voxel responses to concept images. They share much explained variance with a human similarity embedding but miss color, texture and shape dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM representations align partially with human behavioural and neural representations, with gaps on perceptual dimensions (model-to-brain convergence).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, U.S.A., 122 (44) e2512514122 (2025)
record.problems: Cross-model alignment is anchored to LLaMA3-70B, and the text does not give numerical alignment values for individual models. The reported scale-complexity relationship is qualitative and has an acknowledged exception. The model comparison is among language-only next-token-prediction models, not different modalities or objectives.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant measured alignment result was left out. Individual model points in Fig. 3C–D are not separately reported numerically in the text, so they are not recorded as individual rows.

untested.parts: Different training objectives (all models are next-token-prediction base models); non-Transformer architectures (all are decoder-only Transformers); other modalities; other similarity metrics for the cross-model comparison; alignment across training checkpoints (Table S2 lists them, but no cross-model alignment-over-training result is reported).
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
Cross-model alignment uses only Spearman-based RSA at 24 demonstrations on THINGS. Metric and input variations are reported only within LLaMA3-70B.
No analysis of plateau or of shared data or objectives as the cause of convergence.

missing.what: Per-task correlations between alignment with LLaMA3-70B and zero-shot accuracy on 8 benchmarks: ρ 0.693 (CSQA) to 0.856 (ARC-C); e.g. ARC-E 0.848, BoolQ 0.831, HellaSwag 0.849, WinoGrande 0.793.
Parameter count predicts reverse-dictionary accuracy across LLMs (ρ=0.915). This links scale to the capability axis that alignment tracks.

record.verdict_notes: Rows R1–R6 were misassigned to V6: they compare one model to itself across prompts, and the 'absent' states misread rising trends. No V6 or V7 test exists, because cross-model alignment uses a single metric and setting. The V1 evidence is correlational and anchored to one reference model, the best model in the set, so the alignment-capability link is partly built in. No individual cross-model alignment values are given in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Tests language-only models with different architectures, scales and training data, but not models with different objectives or modalities, nor whether cross-modal alignment rises with scale.
No paired image-caption vision-language model comparison.
Runs vary contextual demonstrations, not training initialization seeds; no shared-feature or shared-subspace analysis across seeds.
No mapping between models, layer stitching, relative-representation transfer, or unpaired mapping.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Tests Spearman- and cosine-based RSA, parallelism score, and varying demonstration counts. Does not test other input distributions or out-of-distribution inputs for cross-model alignment.
Does not establish that cross-model alignment plateaus far from complete, or test whether shared training data or objectives cause it.

conditions.value: models above 70% versus models below 50% exact-match accuracy

rows.measure: Qualitative pairwise alignment pattern, visualized by t-SNE from pairwise alignments
rows.value: Models above 70% exact-match accuracy clustered closely; models below 50% showed greater dispersion.
rows.note: The paper states that better-performing models share more similar relational structure, while weaker models diverge.
rows.check: State should be observed, not partial. Strong models clustering while weak models disperse is what V1 predicts (convergence with capability), not a limit on it.

relationships.condition: 67 open-source decoder-only base LLMs of different families, scales and data; Spearman-RSA alignment to LLaMA3-70B at 24 demonstrations, THINGS concepts
relationships.reason: Alignment with LLaMA3-70B correlates with reverse-dictionary accuracy (ρ=0.870, R7) and task-averaged accuracy (ρ=0.831, R8). Models above 70% accuracy cluster while weak models disperse (R10), and higher-complexity models tend to align more (R9).
relationships.display_finding: Alignment with LLaMA3-70B correlated with reverse-dictionary accuracy at ρ = 0.870 and task-averaged accuracy at ρ = 0.831; models above 70% accuracy clustered while weaker models dispersed.
